content:
Owen Phillips: Need a quick call: do we post a Status Page update for the eu-west blip or just put up a docs-site banner + direct comms? Seeing multiple SUPs come in (SUP-1850 + a couple dupes).

incident-bot: Bridge created: #inc-2026-02-08-eu-west-embeddings-timeouts
incident-bot: Incident commander: Rafael Mendes
incident-bot: Related tickets: SUP-1850

Rafael Mendes: IC here. Current scope: eu-west embeddings endpoint elevated timeouts + a few 5xx. Other routes look mostly fine. Impact is >1 customer and still ongoing.

Priya Shah: Support is getting “are you down?” pings already. If we *don’t* status page it, we need a clear one-liner to paste + consistent place to point customers.

Sean Gallagher: +1 to consistent. Per comms alignment doc, status page is for multi-customer service degradation (even if route/region scoped) when we’ve opened an incident bridge.

Elliot Price: Agree. Docs banner is better for “known issue / workaround / long tail” content. For a live degradation, status page is the source of truth, and docs banner can optionally point to it.

Owen Phillips: Can someone link the guidance? Want to make sure we’re not over-posting.

Sean Gallagher: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/customer-incident-comms-alignment (Status page vs docs banner section). TL;DR: if it’s active + multi-customer + we’re paging, do status page. Docs banner only if it’s informational/workaround and not time-sensitive.

Rachel Kim: From the CS side: enterprise accounts expect a status event when there’s region degradation impacting prod traffic. I’d rather post a scoped status note than have customers assume we’re hiding it.

Rafael Mendes: OK. Decision: post Status Page incident as “Investigating” with scope limited to eu-west embeddings timeouts. I’ll own the initial post; Rachel can use it as the canonical reference in customer emails.

Priya Shah: Works. Can we include “workaround: retry w/ backoff; consider switching region if configured” or keep it minimal?

Rafael Mendes: Keep initial status page minimal + factual (symptoms + scope). Once we confirm mitigations, we can add guidance in the next update.

Elliot Price: If we end up with a stable workaround that’s more than “retry,” I can get a short docs banner up that links to the status page + a KB entry, but I don’t want to publish anything until SRE signs off.

Owen Phillips: Great. Rafael, when do you want next update cadence?

Rafael Mendes: Status page update every ~30–60 min while active, sooner if we identify root cause or mitigation lands. I’ll ping here when the post is live.

Statuspage Bot: Status update posted: “Investigating: Elevated timeouts for Embeddings in eu-west”

Rachel Kim: Confirmed I see it. I’ll mirror the language for the 2 enterprise threads and point to the status link.

Priya Shah: I’ll update the SUP-1850 internal note with “status page posted” + link and stop folks from drafting ad hoc explanations.

Owen Phillips: ✅ Thanks all. Decision logged: Status Page for active multi-customer degradation; docs banner only if/when we have validated workaround content.
